mainTopic: Which forbidden items are burned or buried, and why their ashes differ
overview: This amud finishes the משנה's list of forbidden items that must be destroyed. The משנה rules that buried items may not be burned and burned items may not be buried. רבי יהודה allows burning as a stringency, but the חכמים forbid any switch. The גמרא opens with טבי's contradiction: our משנה buries a נזיר's hair and a פטר חמור, but a משנה in ערלה burns a sack woven from them. Three answers are given: a טמא versus a טהור נזיר, a sack versus plain hair (which leads to challenges about ביטול ברוב and pulling out a bird design), and that the ערלה משנה follows רבי יהודה. The גמרא then explains more lines of the משנה: חמץ is burned like רבי יהודה, foods are burned and liquids buried, and רבי יהודה describes how a doubtful bird offering is sent to נחל קדרון. Finally it gives the reason for not switching: buried items have forbidden ashes and burned items have permitted ashes. It defends both halves of that rule against ברייתות, and the chapter and מסכת תמורה close with a הדרן.

steps.title: Burning or burying offerings brought because of a doubt
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that an אשם תלוי and a doubtful חטאת העוף are burned. רבי יהודה disagrees: the אשם תלוי is buried, and the bird is thrown into the אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: An אשם תלוי is burned. רבי יהודה says it is buried. A bird חטאת brought because of a doubt is burned. רבי יהודה says to throw it into the water channel.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of forbidden items and tells us how two offerings brought because of a doubt are destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both offerings come from a doubt, so they cannot simply be eaten or used. The תנא קמא treats them like disqualified offerings that must be burned. רבי יהודה gives each one a different, gentler kind of disposal: burial for the אשם תלוי, and letting the bird wash away in the אמה.

keyTerms.meaning: A provisional guilt offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he sinned
A bird sin offering
Brought because of a doubt
The water channel that ran through the עזרה
Shall be burned / shall be buried

phrases.english: A provisional guilt offering shall be burned.
phrases.notes: This is the offering a person brings when he isn't sure he sinned, so it is 'hanging' in doubt.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: it shall be buried.

phrases.aramaic: חַטַּאת הָעוֹף הַבָּאָה עַל הַסָּפֵק — תִּשָּׂרֵף,
phrases.english: A bird sin offering that comes because of a doubt shall be burned.
Rabbi Yehuda says: one should throw it into the water channel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָשָׁם תָּלוּי — יִשָּׂרֵף, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: יִקָּבֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of items that must be destroyed, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says an אשם תלוי and a doubtful חטאת העוף are burned. רבי יהודה says the אשם תלוי is buried and the bird is thrown into the אמה.

steps.title: The general rule: buried items stay buried, burned items stay burned
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that items meant for burial may not be burned, and items meant for burning may not be buried. רבי יהודה allows burning buried items as a personal stringency.
steps.simpleTranslation: Things that are buried may not be burned, and things that are burned may not be buried. רבי יהודה says that if someone wants to be strict and burn the things meant for burial, he may.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sums up its list with a general rule about not switching the method of destruction. רבי יהודה adds an exception for someone who wants to be strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item has a fixed way of being destroyed. רבי יהודה sees burning as the 'stronger' kind of destruction. So in his view, upgrading from burial to burning is just being extra careful.

keyTerms.meaning: Items that must be buried
Items that must be burned
To take a stringency upon himself
He is permitted

phrases.english: All items that are buried shall not be burned,
and all items that are burned shall not be buried.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
If he wished to be stringent with himself
by burning the items that are buried, he is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּל הַנִּקְבָּרִין — לֹא יִשָּׂרֵפוּ, וְכׇל הַנִּשְׂרָפִין — לֹא יִקָּבֵרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the specific cases into a general rule about the method of destruction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The method of destruction may not be switched. רבי יהודה allows burning buried items as a stringency.

steps.title: The חכמים reject changing the method
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה that a person may not change the method of destruction, even to be strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: one is not allowed to change.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יהודה's exception and say there is no option to switch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, the method of destruction is a fixed הלכה, not a question of 'more' or 'less' strict. So what looks like a stringency to רבי יהודה is, for them, simply doing it wrong. One common explanation is that the ashes of burned items may be used, while the ashes of buried items may not. Switching could therefore lead to a leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: To change (the required method)
It is not permitted

steps.whatToRemember: Every forbidden item has a set method, burning or burial. The חכמים do not allow switching, even as a stringency.

phrases.english: They said to him: one is not permitted to change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's exception from the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יהודה's allowance to burn items meant for burial.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The method of destruction is fixed, so changing it is not counted as a stringency.

steps.title: Is a נזיר's hair buried or burned?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that a נזיר's hair is buried. טבי then asks רב נחמן a contradiction from a משנה in ערלה. There, a sack woven with a נזיר's hair must be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says a נזיר's hair is buried. טבי asked רב נחמן: we learned it is buried, yet another משנה says that if someone weaves a סיט of בכור wool into a garment, the garment is burned. And if he weaves a נזיר's hair or פטר חמור hair into a sack, the sack is burned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by quoting a line from the earlier משנה. It then shows that another משנה seems to say the opposite about the same hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lists a נזיר's hair among the items that are buried. The משנה in ערלה says a sack with a נזיר's hair woven in must be burned. That suggests the hair belongs with the burned items. Given the rule we just learned, that buried and burned items may not be switched, this looks like a direct clash.

keyTerms.meaning: And raise a contradiction against them (one source against another)
The hair of a נזיר
A סיט: the gap between the index and middle fingers when spread
Wool of a firstborn animal, which is forbidden for benefit
A firstborn donkey
Shall be set on fire

steps.confusionAlert: The ערלה source never actually says 'the hair is burned.' It says the sack is burned. The contradiction comes from inferring that the hair inside it belongs with the burned items.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The hair of a nazirite shall be buried.
Tavi raised a contradiction to Rav Naḥman:
We learned: the hair of a nazirite shall be buried,
and raise a contradiction:
phrases.notes: This contradicting source is the משנה in ערלה 3:3.

phrases.english: One who weaves the size of a sit
of wool of a firstborn into a garment,
the garment shall be set on fire;
from the hair of a nazirite or a firstborn donkey into a sack,
the sack shall be set on fire!

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ טָבִי לְרַב נַחְמָן: תְּנַן שְׂעַר הַנָּזִיר יִקָּבֵר, וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens by challenging one item from the משנה's list of buried things.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a נזיר's hair is buried.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ערלה משנה requires burning a sack woven with a נזיר's hair. That implies the hair is an item that is burned, which clashes with the ruling that it is buried.

steps.title: A טמא נזיר versus a טהור נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the two sources are talking about different cases. Our משנה is about a נזיר who became טמא. The ערלה משנה is about a טהור נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: here it is talking about a טמא נזיר, and there it is talking about a טהור נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן settles the contradiction by placing each source on a different kind of נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר who became טמא shaves his head and starts over, and that hair is buried. A טהור נזיר who completes his נזירות puts his shaved hair on the fire under the שלמים (במדבר 6:18). So that hair belongs with the burned items. Both rulings are true, each for its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there: each source deals with a different case
A נזיר who became ritually impure
A ritually pure נזיר who completed his term

steps.whatToRemember: A טמא נזיר's hair is buried. A טהור נזיר's hair is burned, as the תורה commands.

phrases.english: He said to him:
here, with a ritually impure nazirite;
phrases.notes: 'Here' means our משנה, which says the hair is buried.

phrases.english: there, with a ritually pure nazirite.
phrases.notes: 'There' means the ערלה משנה, where the hair is burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כָּאן בְּנָזִיר טָמֵא, כָּאן בְּנָזִיר טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers טבי's contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (כאן... כאן): each source applies to a different kind of נזיר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to discuss the same נזיר hair, so one says buried and the other says burned.
steps.terutzMaskana: A טמא נזיר's hair is buried, and a טהור נזיר's hair is burned.

steps.title: The firstborn donkey contradiction is still unsolved
steps.stepSummary: טבי tells רב נחמן that his answer only fixed the נזיר contradiction. The פטר חמור contradiction is still a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You solved the contradiction between the two נזיר sources. But the contradiction between the two פטר חמור sources is still difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: טבי says that רב נחמן's answer about a טמא and a טהור נזיר only solved half the problem. The same two משניות also clash about a פטר חמור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says a פטר חמור, hair included, is buried. The ערלה משנה lists a sack woven from פטר חמור hair among the things that are burned. The difference between a טמא and a טהור נזיר can't help here, because a donkey has no such status.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male donkey. It is forbidden for benefit if it was not redeemed.
You answered (you solved the contradiction)

phrases.english: He said to him: You resolved the contradiction of nazirite against nazirite,
but firstborn donkey against firstborn donkey is still difficult!
phrases.notes: Our משנה buries the פטר חמור, but the ערלה משנה lists a sack of its hair with the things that get burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁנֵּית נָזִיר אַנָּזִיר, פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר אַפֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that step 5's answer only covers part of the contradiction from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's answer of a טמא versus a טהור נזיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same two משניות also contradict each other about a פטר חמור, and the טמא/טהור distinction cannot apply to a donkey.

steps.title: רב נחמן is silent and asks טבי what he has heard
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן has no answer, so he asks טבי if he has heard an answer from someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was silent and said nothing to him. Then he said to him: Have you heard anything about this?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן doesn't answer. Instead he asks טבי whether he knows of an answer. This sets up the next step, where טבי reports one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing about the law changes here. The step simply admits the question is strong and passes the job of answering to a teaching טבי already heard.

keyTerms.meaning: He was silent
And nothing at all

phrases.aramaic: אִישְׁתִּיק וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי.
phrases.english: He was silent and did not say anything to him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִידֵּי שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ בְּהָא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Have you heard anything about this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִישְׁתִּיק וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב נחמן cannot answer step 6 himself, so he asks טבי for an answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether טבי has heard an answer to the פטר חמור contradiction.

steps.title: רב ששת's answer: a woven sack versus plain hair
steps.stepSummary: טבי quotes רב ששת. The ערלה משנה is about a sack woven from the hair, so it is burned. Our משנה is about plain hair, so it is buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רב ששת said: Here it is talking about a sack, and there it is talking about hair.
steps.whatsHappening: טבי gives רב ששת's answer. The two משניות are talking about different objects: a sack made from the hair, and the hair by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה rules on plain hair, and plain hair is buried. The ערלה משנה is about hair that was already woven into a sack, and that gets burned. This answer works for the פטר חמור, and it could also work for the נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: A sack woven from hair
Hair (by itself, not woven)
Here... there: the two sources are about different cases

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת —
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rav Sheshet said:
Here it is about a sack, there it is about hair.
phrases.notes: The first 'here' means the ערלה משנה, which burns the sack. 'There' means our משנה, which buries the hair.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת כָּאן בְּשַׂק, כָּאן בְּשֵׂעָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 6, as asked for in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: a woven sack versus plain hair
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seemed to be talking about the same thing, the hair of a פטר חמור.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hair woven into a sack is burned. Plain hair is buried.

steps.title: Other אמוראים said both answers too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא gave רב ששת's sack/hair answer, and that רבי אלעזר gave רב נחמן's טהור/טמא נזיר answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also said: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: Here it is about a sack, there it is about hair. רבי אלעזר said: Here it is about a טהור נזיר, there it is about a טמא נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up both answers by showing that other sages said the same things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא matches רב ששת (sack versus hair). רבי אלעזר matches רב נחמן (a טהור versus a טמא נזיר). So each answer has more support behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: A נזיר who is ritually pure
A נזיר who became ritually impure

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
Here it is about a sack, there it is about hair.
Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן — בְּנָזִיר טָהוֹר, כָּאן — בְּנָזִיר טָמֵא.
phrases.english: Here it is about a pure nazirite, there it is about an impure nazirite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answers from steps 5 and 8 with other sages who said the same.
steps.raayaObject: The two answers: sack versus hair, and a טהור versus a טמא נזיר
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא and רבי אלעזר

steps.title: Shouldn't the hair be cancelled by the rest of the sack?
steps.stepSummary: The answer about the sack is challenged. The forbidden hair is only a small part of the sack, so it should be cancelled out by the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Let the sack be cancelled out by the majority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב ששת's answer. If the forbidden hair is just a small part of a sack made mostly of other material, why burn the sack at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a small amount of something forbidden that is mixed into a larger permitted amount is cancelled out. Then the sack would not need to be burned, and the sack answer would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Being cancelled out by a majority: a small forbidden part loses its status inside a larger permitted mixture

phrases.english: He said to him: Let the sack be nullified by the majority!
phrases.notes: He means the forbidden hair should get lost among the rest of the sack's material.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the sack answer from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that a woven sack is burned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A small amount of forbidden hair should be cancelled out by the majority of permitted material, so nothing should need burning.

steps.title: רב פפא: the hair forms a bird design
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the forbidden hair was woven into a bird design, so it stands out and is not cancelled out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is talking about a bird design.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that the case is a sack where the forbidden hair makes a decorative bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A design that stands out on its own is important, so it does not get lost inside the majority. That is why the ערלה משנה could still require burning the sack.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird shape woven into the sack as decoration

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is about a bird design.
phrases.notes: The forbidden hair was woven in as a decorative bird, so it is noticeable and doesn't get lost in the majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a special one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hair was just mixed into the sack and should be cancelled out.
steps.terutzMaskana: The hair forms a separate design that stands out, so it is not cancelled out.

steps.title: Then just pull out the bird design
steps.stepSummary: If the problem is only the bird design, remove it and keep the rest of the sack. Why burn the whole thing?
steps.simpleTranslation: A bird design? Let him pull them out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא. A design can be taken out, so the forbidden part could be removed instead of burning the whole sack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the forbidden part is a separate design, it can be separated out. Then only the design needs to be destroyed, and the rest of the sack should be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him pull them out (remove the forbidden threads)

phrases.english: A bird design? Let him pull them out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the whole sack is burned because of the bird design
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The design can be pulled out, so there is no reason to burn the permitted rest of the sack.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: the ערלה משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says the ערלה משנה follows רבי יהודה, who allows a person to be strict and burn things that should be buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Whose view is this? It is רבי יהודה's, who said: If someone wants to be strict with himself and burn things that are buried, he may.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה tries to explain the burning by saying the ערלה משנה follows רבי יהודה's view from our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 2, רבי יהודה allowed burning buried items as a personal stringency. If the ערלה משנה follows him, the burning there is just an optional stringency. It would not contradict our משנה's ruling to bury.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this?
To be strict with oneself
The items that are supposed to be buried

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: Whose opinion is this?
It is Rabbi Yehuda's, who said:
If he wants to be strict with himself
and burn the items that are buried, he is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 12's question goes unanswered, רבי ירמיה offers another way to resolve the contradiction about burning versus burying the hair.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific sage's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ערלה משנה seemed to require burning as the basic law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The burning follows רבי יהודה's personal stringency.

steps.title: That doesn't answer why the design isn't pulled out
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה's answer is rejected. The question was why not just remove the design, and רבי יהודה's view doesn't answer that.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Our problem is that he should pull them out, and you explain the משנה as רבי יהודה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner pushes away רבי ירמיה's answer because it misses the real question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה only allows being strict and burning things that really need to be destroyed. Here the forbidden design can simply be removed and the rest kept. Even רבי יהודה would not require burning permitted material, so the question from step 12 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: You explain it as (you set the source in a certain view or case)

steps.whatToRemember: The contradiction about a פטר חמור is answered by telling apart a woven sack (burned) from plain hair (buried). Then a chain of challenges follows: why not cancel the hair by majority (it's a bird design), and why not pull the design out. רבי ירמיה's רבי יהודה answer is pushed back here, and the next step shows how he defends it.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה's stringency lets you burn something that has to be destroyed anyway. It does not let you destroy permitted material that could be saved.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: קָא קַשְׁיָא לַן לְשַׁלּוֹפִינְהוּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: Our difficulty is that he should pull them out,
and you establish it according to Rabbi Yehuda?!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא קַשְׁיָא לַן לְשַׁלּוֹפִינְהוּ, וְאַתְּ מוֹקְמַתְּ לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 13's answer, because it does not deal with step 12's question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי ירמיה's explanation that the ערלה משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה's stringency does not explain burning permitted material when the forbidden part can be removed.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה explains his answer is only a fallback
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה clarifies: if the bird design can be pulled out, do that. If it cannot, then the משנה follows רבי יהודה, who allows burning even things that should be buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what I meant: if you can pull out the forbidden threads, good. If not, explain the משנה like רבי יהודה, who said a person may be strict on himself and burn things that only need burying.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה defends his answer from the rejection in step 14. He explains that his רבי יהודה answer was not a reply to the 'pull them out' question. It is a separate way to resolve טבי's contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה says his רבי יהודה answer was never a reply to the 'pull them out' question. If that question can be answered, good, and the sack answer stands. If not, he offers a separate way to settle טבי's original contradiction: the ערלה משנה follows רבי יהודה. In רבי יהודה's view, burning a buried item is an allowed stringency, so burning the hair does not clash with our משנה's ruling to bury it.

keyTerms.meaning: to pull them out (the forbidden threads)
good, fine; that is the best option
set it up; explain the source as following a certain opinion
to be strict on himself
items whose proper disposal is burial

steps.whatToRemember: טבי's contradiction ends with three answers: a טמא versus a טהור נזיר, a sack versus plain hair, and (if the sack answer can't survive the 'pull them out' question) that the ערלה משנה follows רבי יהודה, who lets a person burn things that only need burying.

phrases.english: This is what I meant to say:
If it is possible to pull them out — fine,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the forbidden hair threads woven into the bird design.

phrases.english: and if not — explain it according to רבי יהודה,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אִם רָצָה לְהַחְמִיר עַל עַצְמוֹ
phrases.english: who said: if one wishes to be strict on himself
to burn the things that are to be buried — he is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי ירמיה's answer against the rejection in Step 14 by narrowing when it applies.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the רבי יהודה answer is an independent resolution of the original contradiction, not a reply to the removal question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rejection assumed רבי ירמיה was answering the question of why the bird design isn't simply pulled out.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the removal question can be answered, the sack/hair answer stands. If not, the contradiction is resolved by saying the ערלה משנה follows רבי יהודה, who allows burning items meant for burial as a stringency.

steps.title: The unnamed משנה follows רבי יהודה on burning חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה. It notes that saying חמץ on פסח must be burned matches רבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: these are the things that are burned, and חמץ on פסח is burned. So the unnamed משנה follows רבי יהודה, who said the only way to get rid of חמץ is by burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section, quoting the משנה's list of things that are burned. It points out whose opinion the משנה is following.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known argument about how to get rid of חמץ. רבי יהודה says only by burning, while the חכמים allow any way of destroying it. Since the משנה plainly says חמץ is burned, the גמרא concludes that this unnamed משנה sides with רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: items that must be burned
the תנא taught us without naming anyone; an unnamed statement that matches one opinion
getting rid of חמץ before or during פסח

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean everyone agrees חמץ must be burned. It only shows that this unnamed משנה follows רבי יהודה's side of a debate.

phrases.english: And these are the things that are burned.
The Master said: chametz on Passover shall be burned.
The tanna taught us without naming anyone, following רבי יהודה,
who said: getting rid of chametz is not done
except by burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the sack discussion and begins explaining the משנה's list of items that are burned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The unnamed משנה, which requires burning חמץ, follows רבי יהודה's view that חמץ may only be destroyed by burning.

steps.title: Which items are burned and which are buried?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about impure תרומה and ערלה and asks how to tell which items get burned and which get buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says impure תרומה and ערלה and so on (some are burned and some are buried). How does that work?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and asks a short clarifying question. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that among these forbidden items, the ones meant for burning are burned and the ones meant for burial are buried. But it does not say which are which. The גמרא asks for that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: תרומה that became impure; it may not be eaten
fruit of a tree in its first three years, which is forbidden
how is this? (a request to explain)

phrases.english: Impure teruma and orla, etc.
How is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues down the משנה's list, moving from חמץ to the next items.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which forbidden items count as "to be burned" and which count as "to be buried"?

steps.title: Foods are burned, liquids are buried
steps.stepSummary: The answer: forbidden foods are destroyed by burning, and forbidden liquids are destroyed by burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: Foods are destroyed by burning. Liquids are destroyed by burial.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question with a simple rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The split depends on what kind of item it is. Solid foods get burned. Liquids such as wine or oil get buried. This explains the משנה's vague phrase about some items being burned and others buried.

keyTerms.meaning: foods (solid items)
liquids
burial

steps.whatToRemember: For תרומה טמאה, ערלה, and the like: foods are burned and liquids are buried.

phrases.english: Foods are by burning,
liquids are by burial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question in Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Solid foods are burned and liquids are buried.

steps.title: How רבי יהודה disposes of a doubtful bird sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the חטאת העוף and brings a ברייתא. In it, רבי יהודה describes cutting a doubtful bird sin offering limb by limb and throwing the limbs into the Temple drain, which carries them to נחל קדרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה mentions the bird sin offering. A ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה said, a bird sin offering brought because of a doubt should be thrown into the drain. He cuts it limb by limb, throws the limbs into the drain, and they roll along until they reach נחל קדרון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, the doubtful חטאת העוף. It brings a ברייתא that explains how רבי יהודה's method works in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says this bird should be burned, while רבי יהודה says to throw it into the drain. The ברייתא adds a detail: the bird is first cut into limbs so the pieces can roll away through the drain. The water then carries them out to נחל קדרון.

keyTerms.meaning: a bird sin offering
brought because of a doubt (not sure it was required)
the water channel or drain in the Temple courtyard
cuts it up limb by limb
the Kidron stream outside ירושלים

phrases.english: A bird sin offering, etc.
It was taught: רבי יהודה said:
A bird sin offering that comes due to a doubt —
he should cast it into the drain,
and he cuts it limb by limb,
and throws them into the drain,
and it keeps rolling along to the Kidron stream.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the משנה's list and explains רבי יהודה's view there.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a doubtful חטאת העוף is cut limb by limb and thrown into the Temple drain, which carries it to נחל קדרון.

steps.title: Why may buried items not be burned?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that buried items may not be burned and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'All items that are buried may not be burned.' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks why something that should be buried may not be burned instead. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning destroys an item even more completely than burying it, so it seems it should be allowed. The גמרא wants to know what is wrong with burning.

keyTerms.meaning: Items that must be destroyed by burial
Items that must be destroyed by burning
What is the reason?

phrases.english: All items that are buried shall not be burned, etc.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה after the discussion of the חטאת העוף.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason buried items may not be burned.

steps.title: Ashes of buried items are forbidden, ashes of burned items are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that the ashes of buried items stay forbidden, while the ashes of burned items are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because items that are buried have forbidden ashes, while items that are burned have permitted ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two groups differ in what happens to their ashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ashes from a burned item may be used, but ashes from a buried item stay forbidden. If people burned a buried item, someone might treat its ashes as permitted and use them by mistake. So the חכמים said such items must be buried.

keyTerms.meaning: Their ashes
Forbidden to use or benefit from
Permitted

steps.whatToRemember: The working rule: נקברין have forbidden ashes, and נשרפין have permitted ashes. The rest of this section tests both halves of the rule.

phrases.english: Because items that are buried, their ashes are forbidden,
and items that are burned, their ashes are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Burning a buried item could lead people to use its ashes, which are forbidden. The ashes of burned items are permitted.

steps.title: Challenge: crumbled דם הנדה and בשר המת are pure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the remains of buried items are forbidden, using a ברייתא that calls crumbled דם הנדה and בשר המת pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are the ashes of buried items really forbidden? But a ברייתא teaches: the blood of a נדה and the flesh of a dead person that crumbled are pure. Doesn't that mean they are pure and also permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first half of the rule, that buried items stay forbidden. It brings a ברייתא suggesting that crumbled remains of a buried item are permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead body is something that gets buried. If its flesh, once dried and crumbled, is 'pure' and that means permitted, then the remains of a buried item would not always be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of a woman who is a נדה
Flesh of a dead person
Crumbled into dust
Ritually pure
Doesn't it mean...? (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.english: And are buried items' ashes forbidden?
But it is taught: the blood of a נדה and the flesh of a corpse
that crumbled are pure.
Doesn't this mean they are pure and permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first half of the answer in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the remains of buried items are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls crumbled flesh of a corpse, a buried item, 'pure'. If pure means permitted, the remains of buried items are not forbidden.

steps.title: Pure, but still forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means they are pure but still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. They are pure, but still forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reading from step 22. 'Pure' only means they no longer make a person impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being impure and being forbidden to use are two separate questions. The crumbled flesh stops giving off טומאה, but using it is still not allowed, so the rule about buried items stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And forbidden (to benefit from)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'pure' (טהור) with 'permitted' (מותר). Something can be pure and still be forbidden to use.

phrases.english: No, they are pure but forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Pure' only concerns טומאה. Benefit is still forbidden.

steps.title: Challenge: the crop and feathers of an עולת העוף leave מעילה
steps.stepSummary: רב פנחס challenges from a ברייתא saying the crop and feathers of a bird burnt offering are no longer subject to מעילה once its blood is squeezed out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פנחס objected: with a bird burnt offering whose blood was squeezed out, its crop and feathers are out of the laws of מעילה. Doesn't that mean they are out of מעילה and permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פנחס brings a second attack on the idea that buried items stay forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crop and feathers do not go on the altar. They are disposed of by burial. If 'out of מעילה' means permitted to use, then these buried items would be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird brought as a burnt offering
Its blood was squeezed out on the altar
Its crop (a pouch in the bird's throat)
The sin of using holy property for oneself

phrases.english: רב פנחס objected:
A bird burnt offering whose blood was squeezed out,
its crop and its feathers
have left the laws of מעילה.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לַָאו יָצְאוּ מִידֵי מְעִילָה וּמוּתָּרִין?
phrases.english: Doesn't this mean they have left מעילה and are permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the same claim from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the remains of buried items are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The crop and feathers are buried items. If being free of מעילה means permitted, then buried items can be permitted.

steps.title: Out of מעילה, but still forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the crop and feathers are free of מעילה but still forbidden to use.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. They are out of the laws of מעילה, but still forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of answer as before. Leaving מעילה does not make something permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the offering's main service is done, a person who uses these parts no longer violates מעילה. Using them is still forbidden, though, so buried items keep their forbidden status.

keyTerms.meaning: Have left the category of

steps.whatToRemember: Both ברייתות fail to disprove the rule. 'Pure' and 'out of מעילה' do not mean 'permitted', so buried items stay forbidden.

phrases.english: No, they have left the laws of מעילה but are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פנחס's challenge from step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving מעילה means the items are permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no מעילה, but benefit is still forbidden.

steps.title: Challenge: ashes of הקדש are forbidden forever
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second half of the rule, that burned items have permitted ashes, using a ברייתא saying ashes of הקדש are always forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are the ashes of burned הקדש items really permitted? But a ברייתא teaches: all burned items have permitted ashes, except the ashes of an אשירה, and ashes of הקדש are forbidden forever!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the other half of the rule from step 21. Steps 29 and 30 answer this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many of the burned items in our משנה are holy items, הקדש. If the ashes of הקדש are always forbidden, then burned items do not always have permitted ashes. That weakens the reason given for not burning buried items.

keyTerms.meaning: Property given to the Temple
A tree worshipped as idolatry
Ash
Forever, always

phrases.english: And are burned items of הקדש permitted in their ashes?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא תַּנְיָא: כׇּל הַנִּשְׂרָפִין אֶפְרָם מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: But it is taught: all burned items, their ashes are permitted,
except for the ashes of an אשירה,
and the ashes of הקדש are forbidden forever!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִשְׂרָפִין דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ אֶפְרָן מוּתָּר? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the first half of the rule, the גמרא challenges its second half.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ashes of burned items, including הקדש, are permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the ashes of הקדש are forbidden forever, which goes against the claim that burned items have permitted ashes.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא lists אשירה and הקדש separately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא did not group אשירה and הקדש together because an אשירה can be nullified by a gentile, while הקדש can never be nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason the ברייתא did not join them into one line is that an אשירה can be nullified by a gentile, but הקדש can never be nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: Before finishing its question, the גמרא pauses to explain a small wording detail: why the ברייתא gave אשירה and הקדש two separate lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא could have said 'ashes of אשירה and הקדש are forbidden' in one sentence. It kept them apart because they are not the same: an אשירה can become permitted if a gentile nullifies it, but הקדש has no way to be nullified. This side point sets up the main challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree that is worshipped as an idol
Nullification, which cancels an item's forbidden status
Property consecrated to the בית המקדש
Ever, permanently

phrases.english: And the reason he did not combine them
phrases.notes: He means: why did the ברייתא give the אשירה and הקדש two separate lines instead of one?

phrases.english: and teach them together,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דַּאֲשֵׁירָה יֵשׁ לָהּ בְּטִילָה בְּגוֹי,
phrases.english: is because an asherah can be nullified by a gentile,
but consecrated property can never be nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִיעְרָב הוּא דְּלָא קָעָרֵיב לְהוּ וְתָנֵי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side explanation of the ברייתא quoted in step 26, given before the challenge is stated in full.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אשירה can be nullified by a gentile; הקדש can never be nullified, so the ברייתא lists them separately.

steps.title: The ברייתא says ashes of הקדש are forbidden forever
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states its challenge in full: the ברייתא teaches that ashes of הקדש are forbidden forever, which goes against the rule that burned items leave permitted ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches that ash of הקדש is forbidden forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns from its side point and states the challenge clearly: the ברייתא says ashes of הקדש are always forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule under discussion says that items which must be burned leave ashes that are permitted. This ברייתא says the opposite for הקדש: its ash stays forbidden forever. So the rule seems to be wrong, at least for הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In any case, it teaches', used to point back to the key line of a source
Ash
Forbidden forever

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:
the ash of consecrated property is forbidden forever.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that step 26 began, after the side explanation in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that items which are burned have permitted ashes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the ash of הקדש is forbidden forever, so burning does not always make the ash permitted.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: a fire that started by itself
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא answers that the ברייתא is about הקדש wood that caught fire by itself. Nobody committed מעילה, so nothing turned the ash into חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: the ברייתא means a case where a fire fell on הקדש wood by itself. Since no one knows who did it, there is no person who committed מעילה, and so nothing makes the ash go out to חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא defends the rule by narrowing the ברייתא to one special case: the fire started on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person burns הקדש, he commits מעילה, and that misuse takes the item out to חולין, so the ash is permitted. When the fire starts by itself, no person misused anything. So the ash keeps its holiness and stays forbidden. The general rule still stands; this case is just an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: A fire
By itself, with no person causing it
Misusing הקדש, which takes the item out of its holy status
Non-sacred, ordinary status

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said:
For example, where a fire fell
on consecrated wood by itself,
since it is not known who did it,
there is no person who committed misuse,
that would make their ash go out to non-sacred status.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: כְּגוֹן דְּנָפְלָה דְּלֵיקָה בַּעֲצֵי הֶקְדֵּשׁ מֵאֵלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 28 by limiting the ברייתא to a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the ברייתא is limited to a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that all burned הקדש leaves forbidden ash.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only הקדש that burned by itself, with no person committing מעילה, leaves forbidden ash; when a person burns it, the מעילה makes the ash חולין.

steps.title: רב שמעיה: the ברייתא is about תרומת הדשן
steps.stepSummary: רב שמעיה gives a different answer: the ברייתא speaks about תרומת הדשן, the ash removed from the מזבח, which is forbidden forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמעיה said: when this ברייתא was taught, it was about תרומת הדשן, which is forbidden forever.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמעיה offers a second, separate way to answer the challenge: the ברייתא is not about ordinary burned הקדש at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא explained the ברייתא as a case of fire with no human cause. רב שמעיה instead says the ברייתא is about one special kind of ash, תרומת הדשן, which has its own law of being forbidden forever. Either way, the general rule about permitted ashes survives.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily removal of some ash from the מזבח, placed beside it
A ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: Rav Shemaya said:
When this baraita was taught,
it was taught about the removal of the ashes,
which is forbidden forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שְׁמַעְיָה אָמַר: כִּי תַּנְיָא הָא מַתְנִיתָא בִּתְרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 28, different from רמי בר חמא's answer in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the subject of the source: it refers to a special type of ash
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to speak about all ashes of הקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks only about תרומת הדשן, which has its own rule of being forbidden forever.

steps.title: Proof from ״וְשָׂמוֹ״ that תרומת הדשן stays forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רב שמעיה with a ברייתא that learns three laws from ״וְשָׂמוֹ״: the ash is put down gently, all of it, and without scattering.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And he shall put it' means gently; 'and he shall put it' means all of it; 'and he shall put it' means he should not scatter it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the פסוק of תרומת הדשן to show that this ash keeps its holy status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה requires the ash to be set down carefully, all of it, in one place, and not scattered. These rules show that the ash is still treated as holy after burning. That fits רב שמעיה's claim that תרומת הדשן is forbidden forever.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall put it', from the פסוק about תרומת הדשן
Gently, calmly
Scatter

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers protect the rule that burned items leave permitted ashes: רמי בר חמא says the forbidden ash is from a fire that started by itself, with no מעילה; רב שמעיה says it is תרומת הדשן, which the תורה treats as holy forever.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
'And he shall put it' — gently,
'And he shall put it' — all of it,
'And he shall put it' — that he should not scatter it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב שמעיה's answer in step 30 with a source.
steps.raayaObject: רב שמעיה's claim that the ash of תרומת הדשן is forbidden forever.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that learns from ״וְשָׂמוֹ״ (ויקרא 6:3) that the ash must be set down gently, entirely, and without scattering.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing יש בקדשי מזבח and finishing מסכת תמורה
steps.stepSummary: The traditional הדרן formula closes the chapter יש בקדשי מזבח and declares that מסכת תמורה is finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter יש בקדשי מזבח, and מסכת תמורה is now complete.
steps.whatsHappening: There is no new argument here. This is the closing line that marks the end of the chapter and of the whole מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן עלך means "we will return to you." It expresses the learner's hope to come back to this chapter again. Because this is the last chapter of תמורה, the line adds that the entire מסכת is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: "We will return to you." The closing words said at the end of a chapter
Holy items set aside for the altar, which is the theme of this chapter's opening
"Is finished" or "is completed"
The tractate dealing with exchanging one קרבן animal for another

steps.whatToRemember: The chapter יש בקדשי מזבח ends with the rules about which forbidden items are buried and which are burned, including the ashes of הקדש. With this line, all of מסכת תמורה is complete.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "There is among the holy items of the altar"
and tractate תמורה is completed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the chapter right after the ראיה supporting רב שמעיה's explanation about תרומת הדשן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter יש בקדשי מזבח is closed, and with it the entire מסכת תמורה.
